title.sl: Glagoli s to ali -ing: decided to, enjoy walking
title.de: Verben mit to oder -ing: decided to, enjoy walking
title.it: Verbi con to o -ing: decided to, enjoy walking
title.en: Verb patterns: decided to, enjoy walking

rule.sl:
Za nekaterimi glagoli je **to** + osnovna oblika: **decide, want, hope, promise, agree, refuse, offer, learn, need**: **I decided to go.** (Odločil sem se, da grem.) Za drugimi je **-ing**: **enjoy, finish, mind, keep, avoid, practise, suggest, miss**: **I enjoy walking.** (Rad hodim.) Povedati se je treba po glagolu; pravila ni.

**like, love, hate, start, begin, continue, prefer** vzamejo oboje: **It started raining.** = **It started to rain.** Po **would like** samo to: **I'd like to go.** Pri **stop** in **remember** se pomen spremeni: **Stop talking!** (nehaj) in **We stopped to talk.** (da bi se pogovorili); **Remember to feed the hens.** (ne pozabi) in **I remember seeing him.** (spomnim se).

Za predlogom je vedno **-ing**: **good at walking**, **tired of waiting**, **before eating**, **without paying**, **looking forward to seeing you**.

**want, ask, tell, need, help, would like** + oseba + **to**: **I want you to go.** (Hočem, da greš.) Slovenski *da* tu ni that. **let** in **make** brez to: **Let me help.** V govoru je tudi **I'll try and come.** za I'll try to come.
rule.de:
Nach manchen Verben kommt **to** + Grundform: **decide, want, hope, promise, agree, refuse, offer, learn, need**: **I decided to go.** (Ich habe beschlossen zu gehen.) Nach anderen **-ing**: **enjoy, finish, mind, keep, avoid, practise, suggest, miss**: **I enjoy walking.** (Ich gehe gern zu Fuß.) Eine Regel gibt es nicht, du lernst es mit dem Verb.

**like, love, hate, start, begin, continue, prefer** nehmen beides: **It started raining.** = **It started to rain.** Nach **would like** nur to: **I'd like to go.** Bei **stop** und **remember** ändert sich die Bedeutung: **Stop talking!** (hör auf) und **We stopped to talk.** (um zu reden); **Remember to feed the hens.** (vergiss nicht) und **I remember seeing him.** (ich erinnere mich).

Nach einer Präposition steht immer **-ing**: **good at walking**, **tired of waiting**, **before eating**, **without paying**, **looking forward to seeing you**.

**want, ask, tell, need, help, would like** + Person + **to**: **I want you to go.** (Ich will, dass du gehst.) Deutsches *dass* ist hier nicht that. **let** und **make** ohne to: **Let me help.** Gesprochen auch **I'll try and come.** für I'll try to come.
rule.it:
Dopo alcuni verbi viene **to** + la forma base: **decide, want, hope, promise, agree, refuse, offer, learn, need**: **I decided to go.** (Ho deciso di andare.) Dopo altri **-ing**: **enjoy, finish, mind, keep, avoid, practise, suggest, miss**: **I enjoy walking.** (Mi piace camminare.) Una regola non c'è: si impara con il verbo.

**like, love, hate, start, begin, continue, prefer** prendono tutti e due: **It started raining.** = **It started to rain.** Dopo **would like** solo to: **I'd like to go.** Con **stop** e **remember** cambia il significato: **Stop talking!** (smetti) e **We stopped to talk.** (per parlare); **Remember to feed the hens.** (non dimenticare) e **I remember seeing him.** (mi ricordo).

Dopo una preposizione c'è sempre **-ing**: **good at walking**, **tired of waiting**, **before eating**, **without paying**, **looking forward to seeing you**.

**want, ask, tell, need, help, would like** + persona + **to**: **I want you to go.** (Voglio che tu vada.) *che* qui non è that. **let** e **make** senza to: **Let me help.** A voce anche **I'll try and come.** per I'll try to come.
rule.en:
After some verbs comes **to** + the base form: **decide, want, hope, promise, agree, refuse, offer, learn, need**: **I decided to go.** After others **-ing**: **enjoy, finish, mind, keep, avoid, practise, suggest, miss**: **I enjoy walking.** There's no rule: learn it with the verb.

**like, love, hate, start, begin, continue, prefer** take both: **It started raining.** = **It started to rain.** After **would like** only to: **I'd like to go.** With **stop** and **remember** the meaning changes: **Stop talking!** and **We stopped to talk.**; **Remember to feed the hens.** and **I remember seeing him.**

After a small word like at, of or before there is always **-ing**: **good at walking**, **tired of waiting**, **before eating**, **without paying**, **looking forward to seeing you**.

**want, ask, tell, need, help, would like** + someone + **to**: **I want you to go.** **let** and **make** take no to: **Let me help.** In talk also **I'll try and come.** for I'll try to come.
